quest.title: Upon a Flowery Field of Grass
quest.description: The owner of the flower garden has encountered a small problem...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x15000, Hero's Wit x2, Recipe: Tasses Ragout x1

dialogues.text: Villains... You recalcitrant villains! That's right, run, run far, far away! To the other side of the mountain, to the city alleys — and make sure I don't see you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wha... What's going on?
Hmph. Nothing serious. Hero ran away again. It happens all the time — just say the word "inspection," and off Hero takes...

This time, Prince and Princess fled too... Had I not tripped when taking care of the flower field previously, leaving me with a yet-unhealed leg injury, dealing with those three rascals would've been easy.
Are you mountaineers? If you'd like a place to rest your feet, you can sit awhile in the house — I shall treat you in a bit once I have brought those three rapscallions back by their scruffs.

choices.text: Yes, and we have vowed to conquer every high peak in Teyvat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, we vowed that? Paimon definitely wasn't consulted!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, let's introduce ourselves all the same! Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers — and if you're looking for people, there's no one more experienced than us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If your legs aren't feeling too good, leave the searching to us!
Adventurers... Then why don't you wear those green uniforms?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not everyone has to wear that outfit. Or rather, we're such experienced adventurers that we can just wear whatever we want.
Hmm. I see. I suppose that the services of seasoned adventurers should also come with the requisite payment.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Alright then, good children, call me Earnshaw. I would be most grateful for your help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're looking for... Hero, Prince, and Princess? These don't sound like normal names... Are these nicknames for kids?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: They're dogs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Th—They, uh, sound like... rather kiddy names?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: My daughter named them. If it was not for her raising hue and cry, I would not have raised such delicate creatures.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: When they were still pups, they were quite silly and rather cute, but they quickly grew into disobedient little rascals. Try to control them a little, and ah, they resist and they flee.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: They don't go very far, of course, but one does need to retrieve them all the same. Ah, for a "Hero" to fear something like a tooth inspection... What a joke.

choices.text: Won't they come back once they get hungry?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Or they might awaken the wild spirit in their blood, return to the mountain forests, and become apex predators! That would be a pretty cool story, wouldn't it?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: No, no, rules must remain rules. If we let them off once, they will do this a second and third time. And once they get used to doing ill, they will not change for the better easily.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But they're just little doggies, aren't they? Do we really have to be so strict with them?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Well, they do have a bad example to follow. That silly daughter of mine left home several years ago and hasn't returned. Well, if they had done exactly as she had, that would have saved me some time!

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: But if she were to return and find her precious dogs, whom she raised hell just to own, gone, she'd bawl for all she's worth... Even though this is all her fault, anyway.

choices.text: (Sounds like we've walked into a family issue.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then... So we just need to bring them back home, right?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Yes. The forests are dangerous, and get even more so at night. Those dogs do not know how delicate they are. Even if they do not love it, they are safer in here.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Hero's run off to the north. For an old dog to still be so playful... Seriously...

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: It also likes pausing to forage for food along the path. Don't go easy on it. It'll get in real trouble if it eats something bad.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: If it refuses to leave, harden your heart and <color=#00E1FFFF>take the food it got from Archon-knows-where away</color>. That should give it the signal that it's time to go home.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: The other two haven't gone far. They're just mucking about in the flower garden. Just tell them to get back here, and that should do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, this sounds simple. Just leave it to us! You just wait here, Earnshaw. We'll be right back.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>Careful about the flowers, by the way. Don't tread on them.</color>

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Gotcha, we will! <color=#00E1FFFF>Don't tread on the flowers</color>, right? Well, never mind Paimon, but {NICKNAME}'s pretty agile too.

choices.text: They will probably just play until sundown before returning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes! there's no place like home, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, and we definitely wouldn't sidetrack from our original goal because "the mountain was just there" or something like that!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #Oh! It's {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lanoire, Earnshaw! It's great to see you again!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are you adjusting to life in your new home?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #Don't be silly, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}! This isn't my new home, it's my old home. Isn't that what Cater said?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Grandpa's Tasses Ragout is so tasty! He's teaching me how to make it, but it'll take awhile before I've got it down...

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: There's plenty of time, no need to rush it.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: That reminds me, is this "Cater" not with you? I still haven't thanked him in person...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He had something else to take care of, so we've parted ways for now.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: I see, that's too bad.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Do you think he's already forgotten about me, Ms. Paimon...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course not! He's just tied up with something right now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Besides... You two promised each other, right? The next time you meet, he'll finish telling that story from before, and you'll have lots of amazing stories to tell him, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Yeah... But...

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Ahem! That reminds me, Hero has gone and wandered off and gone who-knows-where again. Lanoire, would you be a good girl and help Grandpa find him and bring him home?

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: I bet he's gotten himself all dirty playing outside. Bring him back and give him a bath.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Aww, just let him play outside. It's boring just staying inside all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Well, if he runs off or gets snatched by a monster in the forest and can't come back, don't come crying to me.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Eek... I—I'll bring him back and give him a bath then!

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Wonderful. Prince and Princess are playing in the garden right now, why don't you bring them back in, too? They're also probably covered head-to-toe in mud by now. I'll give them a good scrubbing later as well.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #Alrighty. {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, you guys rest a while. I'll be right back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why don't we go with you? It'll be just like when we went on adventures in the Fortress.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: You wanna come with me? That would be great!

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Let me think... then let's call this adventure "Operation Rescue Hero"!

choices.text: Heroes should be able to get themselves out of trouble on their own.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: But he's just a doggy, and an old one at that! So, it's up to us brave young warriors to rescue him from the dust and mud!

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: You can go together, just remember not to let Hero eat anything too strange. He more than likely ran off to the north hut to play, if you head north you should run into him.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Okay! <color=#00E1FFFF>If he acts up and doesn't want to come home with us, I'll just take his food away</color>. Then he'll definitely be a good boy and come home!

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Excellent. Also, <color=#00E1FFFF>don't trample the flowers behind the fence</color>!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #Well, you definitely don't have to worry about Ms. Paimon stepping on any! But don't worry, Grandpa. {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and I will be careful.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, let's go!

choices.text: And what about Prince and Princess?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Well... the name would be too long if we tried put them all in! Let's just say that rescuing Hero includes bringing Prince and Princess back inside too.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Great. You kids play with Lanoire for a little while.

talks.objective: Bring Hero, Prince, and Princess home
Bring Hero, Prince, and Princess home
Bring Hero, Prince, and Princess home

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Good children, I'm relying on you to bring those three rapscallions back.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: So, this is the home I didn't know about that Cater talked about.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Welcome home, child. I'm just glad you're back...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought that this would be easier... Who knew they'd be so capricious...

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Well then, children, I hope you now understand that the more capricious they are, the more we need to teach them the rules.

choices.text: Well, we at least remembered not to tread on the flowers...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If only you could also fly, eh? That would've made things way easier.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Well, if you're tired, rest here a while before going. Come, have some of this Tasses Ragout I just made while you're at it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, goodies! But... Oh, we shouldn't. This doesn't seem right.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Come now, do you not trust my skills? I would not speak for other dishes, but I'm very confident in my Ragout, at least.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, Paimon's wondering if this would count as not following the rules or something...

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Labor deserves a reward, so this is what you are owed for your efforts. You need to eat to keep your strength up, after all. And you are adventurers... so you'll need that energy all the more.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: As for your payment for the official commission, I will give it to you later — I believe the Guild's rules indicate as much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe! In that case, don't mind if we do!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: At the old man's invitation, the two of you enjoy some Ragout. While it is not exactly a masterpiece, it warms the soul nonetheless, wiping your fatigue away...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A meal after some honest work always tastes especially great. And the Ragout was... Well, it had a real "homey" feel, eh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, the ingredients and the method of cooking were nothing quite curious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup. It was normal but tastes really good!

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Of course. Even my silly daughter has naught but praises for this dish. Just a whiff of it would send her running to the table, putting all her complaints aside.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: But she's very far away now, and I fear she can't smell my Ragout any longer — I'd wager that she's even forgotten the way home, in fact.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Y'know, Earnshaw, if you don't mind telling us what she looks like, we could find her for you. We're good at that, remember?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If we meet her in our travels, that is.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Ah, you truly are good-hearted children. Thank you. In truth, it would not be hard for me to find her — she did get someone to send me some letters previously.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: But I reckon she doesn't think she's at fault... Why else would she only send letters but not return home?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: As such, I haven't read a single one of her letters. In fact, I haven't opened a single one. We can overlook the folly of animals, but are we to accept that from a human — a grown woman, no less?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Speaking of which, she hasn't sent any letters recently... Perhaps she's finally grown tired of trying to get a rise out of me.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Regardless, I shall not hire people specifically to bring her back. She can either admit fault and return herself, or not at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: O—Okay, if you say so...

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: All the same, thank you for helping to bring Hero and the others back. The payment isn't much, even with the Ragout added in... So take both, would you?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: You adventurers often sleep out in the wild, don't you? Well, remember to eat well and dress warmly. Don't starve, or catch a chill.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup. You take care of your leg too, Earnshaw!

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: See you. Take good care of yourselves!

choices.text: Looks like we need a few rules laid down just for you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? C'mon, Paimon's not like that... Nor is she some kinda disobedient pet!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This operation... is trickier than Paimon expected.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: That's because the giant in the garden really loves those little purple flowers, and he has all kinds of rules.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Unruly children should learn to follow the rules while they're still young. It's even harder to teach an old dog new tricks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's that got to do with Paimon? She's not an unruly child. Hmph!

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Have you all tired yourselves out? I just happened to make some Tasses Ragout today, please, sit down and have some.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #Yes, yes! {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, let's eat together!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Alright! We couldn't turn down an invitation like that from Lanoire, could we, {NICKNAME}? Hehe.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks for your hospitality.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: You're Lanoire's friends, no need to be so polite.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Having been invited inside, you enjoy a simple but delicious meal of Tasses Ragout.\nOver the meal, you share stories from your journey that astonish the old man and make the little girl burst out laughing.\nA joyful time passes amid conversation and laughter...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: What do you think? Isn't Grandpa's cooking even better than Wolsey's?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, guess what! I helped, too!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Though for now I can only help a little bit, Grandpa says that as long as I practice, I'll also being able to make Delicious Tasses Ragout someday!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Hehe, when that day comes, you'll both have to come back and try it for yourselves!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Deal! Paimon's looking forward to it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, it's probably time we got going. Thank you for having us.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: What? You're leaving already?

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: Now, now, Lanoire. They have their own matters to attend to, they can't play with you all the time.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Oh... okay then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't be sad, we'll see each other the next chance we get!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Really? Will Cater be there too next time?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... that shouldn't be completely impossible!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Alright, then. I'll be sure to have lots of amazing stories to tell you all the next time we see each other.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds good. Paimon's sure Caterpillar is looking forward to hearing them, too.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: You're great kids, thanks for coming to see Lanoire and keeping her company. Here's some Tasses Ragout for the road.

response.speaker: Earnshaw
response.text: You adventurers often sleep out in the wild, don't you? Well, remember to eat well and dress warmly. Don't starve, or catch a chill.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We will! You be sure to look after yourselves, as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks Earnshaw's Tasses Ragout is way more delicious! It tastes like... home, if that makes sense?

choices.text: Unruly children get locked up in the garden.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, but Paimon's definitely not gonna step on any flowers! Besides, she could fly over a high wall without a witch's help!
